title: Unidentified object crosses into Latvia as Ukraine resumes refinery strikes; spillover rung holds at 4
bottom_line: Spillover risk is unchanged at rung 4 (deadly or deliberate incident). That rung rests on four Russian drone strikes on merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria in October. No new incident met our logging threshold in the window. On 1 November Latvia's armed forces tracked an unidentified flying object over Ludza and Krāslava for 17 minutes and used a BLAZE interceptor drone for the first time. The object's origin is unknown. Ukraine struck the Kstovo refinery and, by Zelensky's account, a Rostov missile plant despite US pressure. The 30-day chance of a step up to rung 5 stays remote (5%).

ladder.rationale: Rung 4 rests on four Russian drone strikes on merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria between 5 and 23 October that killed crew. No incident was logged today. Rung 5 needs deliberate, sustained Russian action against a NATO or EU state, and nothing in the window points to it.

pathways.rationale: Base: 8 incidents in 30 days against a 12.7-a-month baseline; no serious incident in 12 months. The Latvian intrusion of an unidentified object is not logged and does not change the odds. Unchanged at 15%.
Base: 1 incident in 30 days against 1.3 a month; 2 serious incidents in 12 months. We found no new incident, arrest or attribution in the window. Unchanged.
Base: 4 incidents in 30 days against 1.3 a month; 12 serious in 12 months. No strike in European waters in the window, but Rybar signals the Black Sea shipping campaign continues. Unchanged at 70%.
Base: no incidents in 30 days against 0.7 a month; none serious in 12 months. Hacks of civil-alert apps hit Ukraine and Russia, not Europe. Unchanged.
Base: no incidents in 30 days and no serious incident since 2022. The Kaliningrad radar report is a capability signal, not a sign of a border crossing. Unchanged.
Base: no incidents in 30 days against 0.3 a month. The fake Oreshnik and nuclear alerts were hacks, not state signalling. We found no IAEA plant-safety update in the window. Unchanged.
Base: 1 incident in 30 days; no serious incident since 2022. Bulgaria's runoff is a domestic vote, not an exposed Russian operation. Unchanged.

One above the floor of 1. An unidentified object entered Latvian airspace on 1 November, and the armed forces reported drone wreckage found on 24 October. Neither is logged yet.
One above the floor of 1. GPS interference over the Baltic is persistent (ind-gnss-baltic active). There was no new Estonian incident in the window.

developments.headline: Unidentified object enters Latvian airspace near Russian border; Latvia uses BLAZE interceptor drone for the first time
developments.summary: Latvia's National Armed Forces alerted residents of Ludza and Krāslava at 18:57 on 1 November after an unidentified flying object entered near the Russian and Belarusian borders. It left across the Russian border at 19:16. Latvia launched a BLAZE interceptor drone, its first operational use, then self-destructed it near the border. Defence Minister Raivis Melnis said monitoring continues. Neither the object's type nor its origin has been confirmed, so it is not logged.

developments.headline: Ukraine resumes refinery strikes and claims hit on Rostov missile plant despite US pressure
developments.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Lukoil refinery at Kstovo on 1 November. Nizhny Novgorod governor Gleb Nikitin said more than 100 drones were destroyed and an 'industrial enterprise' suffered significant damage, according to AFP via Digi24. President Zelensky said Ukraine hit the Kamensky plant in Rostov Oblast, which he said is involved in missile production, along with a Pantsir-S2 and an S-400 command vehicle. Russia's defence ministry reported downing 47 drones over nine regions.
developments.russian_framing: Governor Nikitin called the target only an 'industrial enterprise'. The Guardian reported the Kremlin as saying Kyiv was 'simply ignoring' US wishes days before the US midterms.

developments.headline: Russian strikes hit power grids in four central and western Ukrainian oblasts
developments.summary: President Zelensky said overnight Russian strikes hit substations, transformers and power lines in Dnipropetrovsk, Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr and Khmelnytskyi oblasts, and that repair crews were working in all of them. Politico reported thousands left without power. Rybar claimed 'hundreds of Gerans' hit targets, many in western regions. We found no report of a drone crossing into Poland, Romania or Moldova in the window.
developments.russian_framing: Rybar, a pro-Kremlin channel, claimed hundreds of Geran drones struck Ukraine and that many targets in western regions were hit.

developments.headline: Oleshky evacuation truce lapses; US cites interest in a limited Black Sea ceasefire
developments.summary: The local ceasefire for evacuating civilians from occupied Oleshky expired on 1 November. Ukraine's General Staff said its forces also evacuated 167 civilians from the right bank of Kherson region under the truce. The Guardian reported Zelensky saying the truce shows de-escalation steps are possible, and US officials saying interest is growing in a limited Black Sea ceasefire.

developments.headline: Hackers hit civil-alert apps in Ukraine and Russia, and Russia's statistics agency
developments.summary: Ukraine's Air Force said its air raid alert system was hacked late on 1 November. For about an hour the Air Alert app pushed false nuclear, chemical and street-fighting warnings in Russian, including one citing Oreshnik. Early on 2 November Russia's emergencies ministry said its app was also hacked. Belarusian Cyber Partisans claimed to have stolen 23 TB from Rosstat, which denies any leak.
developments.russian_framing: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russian government agencies face constant cyberattacks.

developments.headline: Allies fear Trump could cut US troops or NATO funding after a midterm loss
developments.summary: Politico reported that diplomats fear President Trump could move thousands more troops out of Europe or cut NATO funding after the 3 November midterm elections. Such moves would extend the trend tracked by ind-us-posture: the withdrawal of the rotational brigade from Romania, a cancelled rotation to Poland and Romania, and a European force posture review opened in June 2026.

developments.headline: Russia nears completion of a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad
developments.summary: DW reported that Russia is close to finishing what experts believe is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, able to monitor much of Europe. Experts quoted by DW warned it could intensify the military standoff with NATO. The report describes no new force deployment, so we log nothing.

developments.headline: Bulgaria's Moscow-friendly incumbent leads presidential runoff in exit polls
developments.summary: Exit polls after Bulgaria's 1 November runoff put incumbent Iliana Iotova ahead of pro-Western rival Andrei Gyurov by roughly 7 to 9 points. Iotova is backed by Prime Minister Rumen Radev's camp, and Digi24 described her as pro-Russian. Official results were still pending when the window closed.
developments.russian_framing: Rybar said analysts expect Bulgaria's new leadership not to break with the EU line.

categories.text: Ukraine's General Staff reported 191 clashes on 1 November. DeepState mapped a Russian advance near Hoptivka. Kyiv claimed a record 54,400 Russian killed or badly wounded in October.
Kstovo refinery hit on 1 November; the governor acknowledged damage to an 'industrial enterprise' (via AFP). Zelensky claimed a hit on the Kamensky plant in Rostov. Both at verification 1.

Overnight strikes hit power grids in Dnipropetrovsk, Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr and Khmelnytskyi oblasts. We found no official overnight drone and missile totals and no reported crossing into NATO or Moldovan airspace.
The Oleshky truce expired after evacuations. The Guardian reported growing US interest in a limited Black Sea ceasefire. No talks were scheduled.

An unidentified object entered Latvia for 17 minutes; Latvia used a BLAZE interceptor for the first time. Not logged: type and origin unconfirmed. Moldova's defence ministry counted 19 airspace violations in October.
No strike on shipping in Romanian or Bulgarian waters in the window. Rybar, a pro-Kremlin channel, claimed Russian strikes on Black Sea shipping continue.
Civil-alert apps were hacked on both sides, including a fake Oreshnik warning in Ukraine, and Rosstat was breached. Nothing affected a European system, and nothing was logged.
DW reported that a large Russian radar complex in Kaliningrad is nearing completion. We found no new exercise, build-up or border violation.
Bulgaria's Moscow-friendly incumbent, Iliana Iotova, leads the presidential runoff in exit polls. No Russian influence operation was exposed in the window.
Ahead of the 3 November US midterms, Politico reported allied fears of further US troop cuts in Europe or NATO funding cuts. This feeds the active ind-us-posture amplifier.

strikes_new.summary: Zelensky said Ukrainian forces, including the SBU, hit the Kamensky plant, which he said is involved in missile production, plus a Pantsir-S2 and an S-400 command vehicle worth about $70m. Announced 1 November; timing not stated. No Russian confirmation found.

judgement.text:
We assess the 30-day spillover picture is unchanged. The Black Sea shipping campaign remains the most likely route to further deaths, and airspace remains the most frequent source of incidents. Nothing in the window moves any pathway by 5 points.

The Latvian intrusion matters more for where it happened than for what it was. The object came in near the Russian and Belarusian borders and left toward Russia 17 minutes later. Latvia has not identified it. Ukrainian long-range drones diverted by Russian electronic warfare have entered Baltic airspace before, and Ukraine's foreign ministry said the drone that exploded in Lithuania on 18 October was probably one of them. We have not logged it, because our rules log violations by Russian drones or war debris and neither the object's type nor its origin is confirmed. If Latvia's armed forces identify it as a war drone, we will log it at rung 3, which would lift Latvia's floor from 1 to 3. Latvia's first operational use of a BLAZE interceptor shows the Baltic states fielding cheap counter-drone defences. That lowers the cost of each response but does not change how often objects cross.

Ukraine's renewed refinery strikes (Kstovo, after Ufa and Novokuybyshevsk last week) and the Kamensky strike claimed by Zelensky raise the chance of Russian retaliation against energy and port targets in southern and western Ukraine. Those are the strike routes that put drones over Romania, Moldova and Poland. We assess airspace risk stays near the October tempo of eight logged incidents in 30 days rather than rising, because the 1 November strikes on four oblasts produced no reported crossing.

The main scheduled risk is the US midterm elections on 3 November. US troop or funding cuts would amplify every pathway through weaker deterrence, but they would not change 30-day incident odds directly. A limited Black Sea ceasefire is the one development that would most clearly lower the maritime pathway's 70%. On the ceasefire paradox, it would also free Russian drones and munitions for other uses, which we would assess separately.
judgement.change_my_mind: Any of these would raise our airspace, maritime or overall odds: a Latvian or NATO statement that the 1 November object was a Russian military drone; a Russian strike inside Romanian or Bulgarian territorial waters; or a US announcement of troop cuts in Europe after 3 November.

competing_explanations.subject: Unidentified object over Ludza and Krāslava, Latvia, 1 November

hypotheses.label: Ukrainian long-range drone diverted by Russian electronic warfare
hypotheses.assessment: This fits the 18 October Lithuanian case and the refinery strikes the same night. Ukrainian drones route through western Russia, and the object left toward Russia.

hypotheses.label: Russian drone or decoy probing Latvian air defence
hypotheses.assessment: This is consistent with the probing pattern behind assumption A3, but there is no identification, debris or official attribution.

hypotheses.label: Non-military object or false radar track
hypotheses.assessment: A 2024 Latvian alert turned out to be a flock of birds. Here an interceptor was launched, which points to a tracked target, but its nature is unconfirmed.

forecasts_new.question: Will Latvia's armed forces report a drone entering Latvian airspace from Russia or Belarus between 3 November and 2 December 2026?
forecasts_new.resolution_criteria: Yes if Latvia's National Armed Forces or Defence Ministry reports an unmanned aircraft entering Latvian airspace from Russia or Belarus between 3 November and 2 December 2026, whether or not its origin is identified.
forecasts_new.base_rate_note: Latvia reported drone entries or crashes in March, June and August 2026, plus on 24 October and 1 November: about 0.5 a month, or roughly 40% over 30 days. Raised for the late-October cluster.

forecasts_new.question: Will the US government announce a further reduction of US forces in European NATO countries between 3 November and 31 December 2026?
forecasts_new.resolution_criteria: Yes if the White House or Pentagon announces a withdrawal, a cancelled rotation or a permanent reduction of US forces stationed in a European NATO country between 3 November and 31 December 2026.
forecasts_new.base_rate_note: There were two such announcements in about 14 months: the Romania brigade withdrawal and the cancelled Poland–Romania rotation. That is about 25% over two months. Raised for allied fears reported before the midterms.

taiwan: The most direct lesson is Latvia's first operational use of the Latvian-made BLAZE interceptor drone. It is a working example of low-cost counter-drone defence, relevant to Taiwan's need to defeat large drone raids without spending scarce missile interceptors. Second, Ukraine's sustained refinery campaign (Kstovo, Ufa and Novokuybyshevsk within a week) is a live test of long-range drones against energy infrastructure. That matters both for Taiwan's own deterrent options and for defending its LNG terminals and grid. Third, Politico reports allied fears of post-midterm US troop or NATO-funding cuts. A US drawdown in Europe could free some US forces and munitions for the Indo-Pacific, but it would also signal to Beijing that US alliance commitments can be bargained over. How large either effect is depends on decisions not yet taken.

medium_term.question: Will a Russian drone, missile or debris kill anyone on the land territory of a NATO or EU member state between 2 November 2026 and 2 November 2027?
medium_term.text: F-2026-001 (15% over 90 days) compounds to about 45% a year; we round down for a possible winter or ceasefire lull. Only one death has occurred on NATO land since 2022 (Przewodów, caused by a Ukrainian interceptor), but exposure has surged. Airspace incidents run at 12.7 a month over 90 days against 2.7 a month since 2022. Moldova counted 19 violations in October, with six drones exploding on the ground. Watch Russian drone launch volumes, Ukrainian deep strikes that provoke retaliation near the Danube, and eastern-flank air defence. A general ceasefire (F-2026-011, 15%) would cut this estimate sharply.

long_term.question: Will Russia carry out a deliberate, attributable armed attack on the territory of a NATO member by 2 November 2030?
long_term.text: Since 2024, several European intelligence services have publicly assessed that Russia could rebuild enough capability for a limited war with NATO within a few years of the fighting in Ukraine winding down. That is a judgement about capability, not intent. Three observable drivers set our estimate. Russian force regeneration is slowed if Kyiv's claims of record October losses are accurate. European defence spending and munitions output raise the cost of an attack. US posture is under review. A1 holds today, and A5 implies risk rises after a ceasefire. We would move to unlikely (25–35%) on a US drawdown combined with a ceasefire that frees Russian ground forces.

assumptions_check.note: No deliberate, attributable Russian attack on NATO territory. October's deadly ship strikes were part of the campaign against Ukraine-bound shipping, not attacks on states.
assumptions_check.text: Russia avoids deliberate, attributable armed attacks on NATO territory while its main force is committed in Ukraine.

assumptions_check.note: Article 5 commitment unchanged. Allied fears of post-midterm troop or NATO funding cuts (Politico) are a watch point, not yet evidence of weakening.
assumptions_check.text: The United States remains committed to defending NATO allies under Article 5.

assumptions_check.note: October's incursions tracked Russian strike routes. The Latvian object of 1 November is unidentified and fits spillover at least as well as a probe.
assumptions_check.text: Most airspace incidents are spillover from strikes on Ukraine or deliberate probes below the threshold of attack, not preparation for an invasion.

assumptions_check.note: Sabotage attributions continued through October (Romania, Lithuania). No pause linked to the Oleshky truce or US diplomacy.
assumptions_check.text: Russia's covert campaign in Europe (sabotage, cables, jamming) continues regardless of battlefield or diplomatic developments.

assumptions_check.note: The Oleshky truce was local and short and did not test the assumption. US interest in a limited Black Sea ceasefire would be the first relevant test.
assumptions_check.text: A ceasefire in Ukraine would lower near-term incident risk but raise medium-term risk as Russian forces reconstitute near NATO borders.
